Re: Appeal of adverse benefit determination  
Member: Sawyer Delgado  
Member ID: W188500611  
Reference number: POC-C3B5D8F398-85355  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial: August 13, 2026  

To Anthem Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. That conclusion should be reversed because the MRI demonstrates a specific structural lesion that corresponds to my symptoms, examination findings, and neurologic deficit.

The clinical record establishes the following:

- I have had nine months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility exercises, from April 10, 2026, through June 19, 2026. I completed 24 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 14, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- The June 30, 2026, lumbar MRI shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain extending into the right calf and cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on MRI.
- The requested procedure is directed at the documented L4-L5 lesion and compressed L5 nerve root.
- There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or other documented condition that would make the proposed surgery unsafe. I am a nonsmoker, and my BMI is 29.

The imaging is therefore not an isolated or nonspecific finding. It demonstrates severe right lateral recess stenosis and L5 nerve-root compression at the same level that corresponds to my right-sided radicular symptoms and neurologic findings. The objective MRI findings, progressive symptoms, functional limitation, examination, and failed conservative treatment should be reviewed together.

The requested surgery is also medically reasonable after substantial nonoperative treatment. I completed a structured physical-therapy program, used anti-inflammatory medication for four months, and underwent an injection that produced only temporary partial improvement. Despite these measures, my symptoms remain progressive and significantly limit standing and daily function.

The publicly available Carelon spine guideline appears to be a potentially relevant document for lumbar discectomy, foraminotomy, and laminotomy, but Anthem has not confirmed that it is the governing criteria for my New York Commercial/ACA plan or this decision. I have not quoted that document here as the plan’s governing policy. Please identify in writing the exact medical policy or clinical-utilization criteria applied to this request, including the version and effective date, and provide the specific imaging requirement that Anthem believes was not met.

Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030. In the alternative, please conduct a new clinical review based on the complete records, including:

1. The June 30, 2026, lumbar MRI report and images showing the L4-L5 extrusion, severe right lateral recess stenosis, and traversing L5 nerve-root compression;
2. The physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 completed visits from April 10 through June 19, 2026;
3. Medication and injection records documenting inadequate NSAID response and only three weeks of partial relief after the April 14 injection;
4. Examination findings documenting the corresponding neurologic deficit and positive provocative testing; and
5. The surgical assessment from Lindqvist, MD.

If Anthem continues to deny authorization, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the exact criteria applied, the records reviewed, the qualifications of the reviewing clinician, and instructions for any available external review.

Please treat this letter as a timely appeal. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 9, 2027.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Delgado
